text:
Toronto visits Columbus tonight with a slight edge on the scoreboard model, but not in the underlying numbers. The model projects CBJ for 3.24 goals and TOR for 3.02. At five on five, TOR has taken 44% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and CBJ 48%, so both teams have been outchanced more often than not. TOR is also on the second night of a back-to-back after beating SJS 3-1 last night, and it will be without John Tavares (lower body), who is on injured reserve.

The special-teams matchup to watch is TOR's power play, which creates 0.79 expected goals a game against a CBJ penalty kill that allows 0.83. CBJ takes 4.14 penalties a game, which keeps giving opponents chances. In net, projected starters are Anthony Stolarz for TOR and Jet Greaves for CBJ. Goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shot quality predicts) puts Stolarz at -0.87 this season and -6.58 last season, while Greaves sits at +1.97 this season and +15.02 last. Stolarz starts over Sergei Bobrovsky.

Recent form favors TOR, which is 2-2-1 in its last five with 50% of the expected goals, while CBJ is 2-3-0 with 42%. Among players to watch, Auston Matthews plays his 700th game and has a 38% chance to score, with William Nylander at 37% and a 73% chance at a point. Kirill Marchenko returns to Columbus for the first time since leaving, and Matthew Knies faces Toronto for the first time since leaving. The model doesn't price those reunions or the milestone, so they add color rather than a prediction.
